content: User prefers tech-lead reviews to avoid bookkeeping-only "close tracking" actions. Resolved items should be recorded in summary (e.g., resolved-by-decomposition) and excluded from Priority Actions/Persistent Issues.
User wants items they mention to be added one-by-one into knowledge as backlog entries from now on.
Implement thread fork feature.
Implement skill runtime reload feature.
Support using tool plugins directly in TypeScript form without build/package step; reference pi-mono approach for detailed design.
Introduce domain-dedicated tech-lead reviewers (core, runtime, web, tui) instead of only whole-repo review, and run them on GitHub Runner for automated checks.
In TUI, make the plan UI float fixed at the bottom of the viewport.
User wants stale or no-longer-valid knowledge entries to be actively updated or deleted rather than left in place.

Do not store immediately planned implementation intent as knowledge. Anti-pattern: adding a knowledge entry like 'user wants to build some feature' and then immediately saying 'now I will start implementing it.' Knowledge should capture durable preferences, patterns, corrections, discoveries, or actual backlog items worth preserving across sessions, not transient intent for the current turn.
In TUI, when resuming a conversation, do not print the entire past message history; show a bounded/condensed resume view instead.
In the web client, after the user answers a question/request_user_input prompt, the resulting tool block should be rendered in the conversation UI.
For userId fallback, generate a random UUID on first run and persist it for reuse across launches instead of deriving identity from MAC address or other hardware identifiers.
Provide a way to disable unnecessary built-in agents.
Implement micro-compaction: prune old tool results to reduce retained history.
Investigate and fix occasional garbled characters when pasting text in the TUI.

Provider-native web assistant blocks now stream live through assistant message deltas via content_block_delta. TUI/Web should render provider_tool_use, web_search_result, and web_fetch_result as soon as they arrive, while avoiding duplicate re-render on message_end. When replaying persisted provider-native web blocks into Anthropic requests, Anthropic-origin blocks must be converted back to native server_tool_use/web_search_tool_result/web_fetch_tool_result blocks; blocks from other providers should not be sent to Anthropic. For diagnostics, DILIGENT_DEBUG_WEB_TOOLS=1 logs both raw web payload stages ([llm:web-tools]) and emission timing/fallback decisions ([llm:web-tools:emit]) so delayed provider delivery versus completed-response fallback can be distinguished.
User prefers provider-native web blocks to be presented in a UI format similar to ordinary tool calls rather than as a distinct assistant-content style.

Thread resume behavior for tool definitions: if the thread runtime is already in-memory in the current app-server process, resume reuses existing agent/tools (no rebuild). If resumed from persisted state (e.g., after restart or missing in-memory runtime), runtime creation path rebuilds default tools via createRuntimeAgent -> buildDefaultTools.
For the VS Code extension UX, the user prefers the chat surface to live at the same hierarchy level as code editors rather than being confined to the extension sidebar/panel.

For the VS Code extension conversation UI, the user prefers assistant output to render as plain flowing text similar to the TUI rather than boxed block-heavy cards, and wants appropriate collapsible treatment for secondary/detail-heavy sections.

For the VS Code extension, do not introduce a VS Code-specific protocol. It should compose the existing shared protocol and fix current implementation drift before adding higher-level UX enhancements.

Root cause found & fixed for repeated "Anthropic thinking blocks require signature" ProviderError: assistant `thinking` content blocks produced by non-Anthropic providers (chatgpt, gemini, openai-compatible) never carry a `signature` (it's optional in ThinkingBlockSchema). When a thread switches models mid-conversation (e.g. chatgpt-5.5 -> claude-sonnet-5), replaying that history verbatim made `convertAssistantContentBlock` in packages/core/src/llm/provider/anthropic.ts throw on the old thinking block, permanently poisoning the thread — every subsequent user turn failed identically since the offending history entry never gets removed. Fixed by dropping (returning undefined for) assistant thinking blocks without a signature during Anthropic conversion, mirroring the existing pattern for foreign `provider_tool_use` blocks (see anthropic.ts convertAssistantContentBlock, and test packages/core/test/llm/provider/anthropic.test.ts). Confirmed via session log .diligent/sessions/20260701025515091000-a2bde4.jsonl. Note: persisting the user message before the provider call is normal/intended chat behavior and not the actual bug — the recurring failure was caused by permanently-poisoned history, not premature persistence.
